svg.title: Step 3 · How Gemini's answer reaches the page
svg.desc: The page posts the question with the browser's locale and time zone. The chat route checks them, takes the model made when the app started, or says it isn't set up, and builds the system prompt: the rules, the units for the locale, and the visitor's own today and tomorrow. LangChain streams Gemini's answer within the caps: 1,024 tokens and 30 seconds an answer, 20 seconds and two attempts a call. Each word goes to the page as plain text; the finished answer's Markdown becomes safe HTML. A failure becomes our own sentence: busy, too slow, not set up, or no answer. LangSmith traces the run only through the app's own client, which hides its inputs and outputs, and the log line holds the tokens.

A failure, as one of ours
rate limit (429): "busy, try again in a minute"
timeout: "took too long" · bad key: "isn't set up"
anything else: "didn't answer" · with the ref
the model's own error: its class in the logs, only
stream_turn(): as in step 2
the turn; each word as plain text, its line breaks kept
the end: the answer's Markdown made HTML, once:
raw HTML off, pictures off, links in a new tab
chat.done: answerChars, ms, tokensIn, tokensOut, model
Why the caps: on Vercel, Stop never reaches the function (issue 32), so an answer no one reads
still runs to its end; its tokens and its time have a ceiling, whatever happens.
In the tests: tests/fakes.py's stand-in streams a known answer, reports tokens, and fails on cue
LangChain's interface and standard exceptions: the app names no provider but in model.py.
No tools yet: until step 4, the model says it can't check the weather.
